subject: EuroBank: clarifying site-of-record, cross-border compute & egress commitments
messages:
From: Jurgen Schaefer <jurgen.schaefer@eurobank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: EuroBank Security <security@eurobank.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:02:00 +0200
Subject: Questions on EU site-of-record + automatic failover to other regions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Before we move to the SOW stage, our legal and cloud teams asked for clear statements on a few items in your RFI:

1) Can you confirm that persistent customer data (logs, user-provided documents, model fine-tune artifacts, audit trails) can be kept in the EU at rest as the site-of-record?

2) Under heavy load, does Redwood ever route live inference compute to non-EU regions (e.g., US/APAC) by default? If so, is that automatic or opt-in, and what data egress safeguards are in place?

3) For cross-border compute, can we require that cryptographic keys (KMS/HSM) remain in the EU so that no decrypted payload can be stored outside the EU?

4) What audit evidence (logs, signed attestations) can you provide to show compliance if we set strict EU-only residency?

We attached our RFI questions as a PDF (see attached). Would appreciate a short, explicit response we can share with procurement/security.

Best,
Jurgen
Head of Cloud Architecture
EuroBank AG

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jurgen Schaefer <jurgen.schaefer@eurobank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:35:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Questions on EU site-of-record + automatic failover to other regions

Hi Jurgen — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below so you can share with procurement/security.

Executive summary (short):
- Site-of-record: yes — persistent artifacts (storage blobs, SSO audit trails, long-term logs, model artifacts) can be pinned to EU-hosted storage and will not be egressed by Redwood unless you explicitly enable cross-border replication.
- Compute failover: Redwood will not automatically run persistent compute in non-EU regions that result in storage of customer data outside the EU unless the customer enables "cross-border compute" in their tenancy. There are opt-in controls at the tenant level.
- Keys: You can require customer-managed KMS or HSM with keys provisioned and kept in EU regions; Redwood supports envelope encryption with customer KMS.
- Audit evidence: we can provide signed S3/Blob access logs, consolidated request traces for the period you request (retention depends on the plan), and compliance attestations (SOC2 Type II reports).

Details and operational caveats:
1) What we treat as site-of-record: any long-lived storage (model files, uploads, evaluation datasets, billing traces) lives in the region you choose. For EU-only customers we provision EU buckets and database instances. Temporary inference caches (KV cache, prefix cache) are ephemeral and by default allocated in the same region; they are not persisted to long-term storage.

2) Failover behavior: we offer three routing policies you can choose per-route:
  - Strict locality (EU-only): requests are routed only to EU compute; if capacity in EU is exhausted requests queue or return 429/503 depending on your SLA window.
  - Local-first with remote burst: local EU compute preferred; if capacity is exhausted and you have enabled remote-burst, we will route live inference to matched non-EU compute pool for short-lived execution. In this mode we do not write persistent artifacts back to non-EU storage; logs related to routing decisions contain metadata but not PII unless you enable expanded diagnostic exports.
  - Cost-tiered routing with consent: customers can allow cross-border compute for non-sensitive routes and keep sensitive routes EU-only.

3) Key residency: we support (a) customer-managed KMS hosted in EU (recommended for strict residency), (b) Redwood-managed KMS with EU-only key storage (limited to enterprise plans), and (c) HSM integration for FIPS-aligned customers. We never persist decrypted model payloads outside the region if keys remain EU-bound.

4) Audit / evidence: we can provide the following artifacts on request (delivery SLA depends on contract):
  - Signed access logs for storage operations (CSV)
  - Per-request regional routing traces (anonymized by default; can be PII-inclusive under NDA)
  - JSON manifest of deployed model artifacts and their storage locations
  - SOC2 Type II report and penetration test summaries

I attached a short appendix that maps our configuration knobs to typical contractual asks — that should help your legal/procurement draft controls. Marcus and Karthik, see any corrections and please add operational nuances.

Next steps: if EuroBank wants a site-of-record commitment in the SOW, we should document the routing policy and KMS ownership. I can draft a short SOW addendum after we confirm retention windows.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on EU site-of-record + automatic failover to other regions

Jurgen / Sofia — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side that procurement/security often ask about.

- Telemetry and diagnostic logs: by default we collect request-level telemetry (latency, token counts, routing decisions). If EU-only is selected we keep telemetry in EU; exports to third-party monitoring systems are blocked unless explicitly configured in the tenant settings.

- Temporary caches and KV: our KV cache is ephemeral and scoped to the execution host. We do not write KV cache contents to persistent storage. If remote-burst is enabled, the remote execution host receives the input payload in-memory for inference; by design CI/CD artifacts and model checkpoints are not copied to the remote site.

- Egress controls: customers may enable one of two egress behaviors:
  1) Block all cross-border compute (strict) — requests that would route to non-EU compute fail with an explanatory error/status code.
  2) Allow cross-border compute with restricted telemetry — the compute happens in the remote region but (a) we do not persist payloads there, (b) logs emitted from the remote host are limited to non-PII fields unless a Data Transfer Agreement is in place.

- Replay / auditability: for customers requiring full audit trails we can produce a signed, time-bound trace that shows the regional decision path for each request. We retain routing traces for 90 days by default; extended retention is available as an add-on.

- Contract language we suggest for the SOW:
  - "Redwood shall maintain site-of-record within EU (region: eu-west-1/eu-central-1) for all customer-owned persistent data and artifacts unless EuroBank provides written consent for cross-border replication."
  - "Customer-managed KMS: keys must be provisioned in EU; Redwood will use envelope encryption and will not decrypt payloads outside EU-bound hosts when keys are EU-resident."

Happy to walk through any of these live with your cloud/security folks.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
